summary.text: King of Cos whom Homer names in the isle's chief city, and whom Apollodorus makes a son of Poseidon by Astypalaea — slain when Heracles stormed the island by night.

Not to be confused with Eurypylus son of Telephus, the Mysian prince who killed Peneleos at Troy and was slain by Neoptolemus (`eurypylus-telephus`), or with Eurypylus son of Euaemon, lord of Ormenion in the Iliad (`eurypylus-euaemonid`).

story.text: In the Catalogue of Ships Homer counts Cos with Nisyrus, Crapathus, Casus and the Calydnian isles under the sons of Thessalus, but names the place the city of Eurypylus — the eponymous lord of the Dorian isle.

Apollodorus tells a violent end: when Heracles was sailing from Troy, Hera sent storms against him; driven to Cos, he forced his way into the city by night and slew Eurypylus, son of Poseidon by Astypalaea, when the Coans had stoned his ships thinking him a pirate.
